name: Central Station

text: Platforms one to four, in letters a foot high, under a glass roof
you cannot see the far end of.
NORTH: FROSTMERE. THE CROWN LINE. THE HIGH CLIFFS.
Platforms five to nine.
EAST: THE WETLANDS, MIREHAVEN ROAD-HEAD, THE FERRY QUAYS.
SOUTH: THE PASS, EMBERFALL, AND THE WHOLE OF THE COAST.
Platforms ten to fourteen. Goods only, and busier than all the rest.
A board of what has come in this morning: stone, coal, glass, fish,
and eleven crates consigned to a Foundation address with no street on it.
The barrier line. Fourteen gates, all of them staffed, all of them queued.
Beyond it the platforms go on until they stop being platforms
and start being weather.
The booking hall. Nine windows, a queue at every one, and a fare board
in six columns.
Half the destinations on it are places you have never heard of.
Parcels and left luggage. A wall of pigeonholes going up out of reach,
and a ladder on a rail to get at the top of it.
Everything in Caelora passes through this room eventually.
The departure board, and a man on a ladder changing it by hand.
Forty-one departures before midnight.
The northern column has SUSPENDED chalked across it in a hurry.
The arrivals board. LATE, LATE, ON TIME, LATE, and one line reading
simply HELD AT THE TUNNEL.
Nobody is surprised. Two people are furious. It is a station.
The bookstall. Novels, newspapers, timetables, and a rack of postcards
of the Grand Park with the tower behind it.
The top seller is a pamphlet on how to survive a flood. It is free.
A flower stall, doing better trade than the bookstall.
A card explains why: everybody arriving in Aureline is arriving
at somebody, and nobody wants to do it empty-handed.
A bench worn to a hollow at each end and shining in the middle.
A brass plate on the back: GIVEN BY THE PORTERS OF THIS STATION,
FOR PEOPLE WAITING ON NEWS.
A city map under glass, four feet across, and a red dot saying YOU ARE HERE.
The dot is about a third of the way up.
There is more city above the dot than most cities are.

_plan: A station is the fastest way to say a city is enormous: fourteen gates, forty-one departures before midnight, and a map where you are only a third of the way up. The barrier line at y1 is a solid run of gates with three staffed openings, so the player can talk to every gate and board nothing -- Frostmere, Skyreach and Crownspire are Stage 5 and there must be no stub to walk into. The northern column is chalked SUSPENDED, which is a true station answer and also the first cold breath of Act 5.
